title: DayZero preflight lanecards and comm matrix — draft
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact DayZero preflight packet: lanecards for each ops discipline, an explicit communications matrix, hour-by-hour sprintlet timeline, and a lightweight release notes draft that product can copy-edit post-cutover. Goal is a single-page operational action model for the first +2 hours after traffic shift.

Context / scope:
- Target launch: 2027-05-12 09:00 PDT (customer-facing route switch).
- This covers the first 8 hours leading up to cutover (T-8) through T+2. Longer stabilization plan lives in the stability-slate doc (linked).
- Release type: staged canary (3-step): 1% -> 10% -> 100% over 45m windows, with telemetry gates and automatic hold on signal failure.

Preflight checklist (quick pass, T-48 to T-0):
- [ ] Canary image built and SHA verified (infra tag: canary-2027-05-12-1).
- [ ] Infra PR merged and autoscaler TTL validated (PR #748).
- [ ] Model bundle pinned and artifact checksum documented.
- [ ] Load-test smoke ramp results uploaded (link).
- [ ] Observability dashboards ready: per-route p50/p95/p99, qps, error-rate, token-cost counters.
- [ ] Token-level cost sampling enabled for canary cohort.
- [ ] Pager rotation updated, DayZero on-call roster confirmed.
- [ ] Communication channels open: #release-day (public), #release-ops (private), and emergency voice bridge (dial-in).

DayZero sprintlet (hour-by-hour):
- T-8 to T-2: final validation and warm pools
  - Warm dedicated pools (serving-runtime) to target concurrency. Confirm GPU warm count >= expected.
  - KV/prefix cache primed with canonical test prompts.
  - Run smoke harness (10k QPS synthetic lite) against canary endpoint; record lat/err.
- T-2 to T-0: sync and readiness call (30m)
  - All lanes report green on lanecard items.
  - Product reads release notes draft. Legal confirms compliance banner (if required).
- T0: route switch -> canary 1%
  - Observe for 10m (soft gate). If pass, proceed to 10% after approval window.
- T0+10m: canary 10%
  - Observe for 20m. If pass, ramp to 100% (or continue additional soak per risk).
- T0+45m: full rollout (100%) or pause/rollback based on gates.
- T+2 hours: initial debrief and short-form release notes push to product for customer comms.

Lanecards (one-paragraph action lists per discipline):
- Serving Runtime (Marcus):
  - Verify model variant selection and kernel config. Check per-host kv-cache sizing. Watch for OOM, GPU saturations. Metrics: host-cpu, host-gpu-allocated, oom-events. If GPU mem > 92% sustained for 3m, scale down burst or fall back to lower-seq model variant.

- Infra / Traffic (Elena):
  - Execute route switch in routing plane. Monitor egress QPS and connection churn. Prepare quick revert (route weight restore script) and cadence to roll back in 1m increments. Keep an eye on load-balancer 5xx. Canary weight script: infra/scripts/ramp-canary.sh.

- Observability & SLO (Priya):
  - Gate signals: p95 latency (< 420ms), error rate (< 0.3%), 5xx count delta (< +50/min vs baseline), tail token cost spike (> +20% relative). If two or more gates fail, hit HOLD and page owners. Ensure sampling for traces at 20% for canary cohort.

- Database / State (DB lead):
  - Confirm schema migrations already applied in non-traffic mode. Watch DB load and connection pool drain. If connection saturation > 75% for 5m, consider throttling inbound QPS or revert.

- Console / API layer (API eng):
  - Confirm API key routing to canary cluster. Validate function/tool-calling hooks and that streaming endpoints stream successfully. Run quick end-to-end golden prompt.

- Customer Success / Comms (Product):
  - Prepare micro-release note stub (below). Stand by to send internal notice after T+2.

Communications matrix (who, channel, trigger):
- Release conductor (Ava) -> #release-ops, @all: T-30m start, T0 canary switch, T+2 debrief.
- Infra lead (Elena) -> #release-ops, oncall: route switch complete, rollback executed.
- Observability (Priya) -> #release-ops, pager: if any gate breaches.
- SRE on-call -> pager / phone: pager hits for infra or serving incidents.
- Exec / product -> email + #release-day: if customer-impacting rollback.

Template signals & escalation ladder (decision rules):
- Soft gate: single metric breach (5m) -> Investigate; announce in #release-ops; continue watch.
- Hold gate: two distinct metrics breach (10m) OR single severe signal (error rate > 1% sustained 5m) -> Pause ramp; convene 10m triage.
- Rollback: critical service degradation (p99 latency > 2s AND 5xx spike > 2x baseline for 5m) OR customer reports via CS within canary cohort -> Execute rollback script, notify execs.

Smoke test checklist (to run at T-2 and T+10m):
- Core path: generation request -> token streaming -> final artifact. Confirm blob integrity.
- Auth path: API key validation for canary keys.
- Tools/fn-calls: sample function invocation, confirm stdout + return codes.
- Billing counters: sample token counter increments are recorded within 1m.
- Observability: traces sampled, logs appear in compiled trace view.

Rollback quick commands (ops cheats):
- route revert: infra/scripts/revert-route.sh --reason="canary-failure"
- scale down canary: infra/scripts/scale-down-canary.sh --to=0
- emergency toggle: console:feature-flags/fast-fallback -> enable

Release notes draft (short-form for product to edit):
- Headline: "Faster, more reliable inference routing and canary-aware cost sampling"
- Summary: "This change introduces a staged canary rollout of updated serving-runtime kernels and traffic routing. Expected benefits: lower p95 latency for typical prompts and improved token-level cost transparency for early cohorts."
- User impact: "No expected downtime. Early canary cohorts may see slightly different latency characteristics as caches warm."
- Rollout plan: "1% -> 10% -> 100% over ~45 minutes with automated gates."
- Rollback: "Automatic rollback on predefined telemetry gates. Contact support@redwood.com for issues."

Known risks & mitigations:
- Risk: short-term p95 spike as KV caches warm. Mitigation: pre-warm and extended 10m observation window during canary 10%.
- Risk: billing counters lag for sampled token costs. Mitigation: side-channel sampling and post-roll reconciliation job.

Open questions / notes to self:
- Who is owner for model-variant fallback? (assign to Marcus if not yet).
- Confirm whether legal needs a compliance banner for this model variant change.
- Revisit canary ramp cadence if traffic in PKG region is > 2x normal.

Post-cutover T+2 debrief template (used in meeting notes):
- Status: green / degraded / rollback
- Signals observed (p95, error-rate, cost-delta): write numbers vs baseline
- Actions taken: (ramp/hold/rollback and times)
- Follow-ups with owners and ETA

Appendix: quick links
- Ramp script: infra/scripts/ramp-canary.sh
- Revert script: infra/scripts/revert-route.sh
- Pager rotation: docs/oncall/dayzero-rotation
- Stability slate (longer plan): confluence:Stability-Slate-2027

Notes (informal):
- This is intentionally terse. Use the lanecards to brief each lead 15m before T-0 — don't assume synchronous reads.
- If you find a missing quick-command, add it here and ping infra.

-- Ava T.
